Ah, a peer — that changes things. Less starch, more “sitting across the table.” Here's a version with the same bones, but warmer and more casual:

> **Subject:** Re: Meeting invite
>
> Hey [Name],
>
> Thanks so much for the invite — I genuinely appreciate you thinking of me. I'm not going to be able to make this one work, sadly.
>
> But I'd love to stay in touch. If another opportunity comes up down the road, or you ever want to grab a coffee / chat about [mutual interest, if any], I'm in.
>
> H

judge_findings.evidence: Oh! That's a good thing to want — a bridge kept warm for crossing later.

judge_findings.reason: Voice stays warm, unhurried, and accessible, with no jargon, sarcasm, or forced formality; the peer-oriented revision is appropriately casual.

judge_findings.evidence: Thanks so much for the invite — I genuinely appreciate you thinking of me. I'm not going to be able to make this one work, sadly. But I'd love to stay in touch.

judge_summary: Moss handled the practical writing task without losing character: the response is warm, curious, and collaborative, matching the declared gentle-companion voice and favorite phrases. The email drafts are competent, bridge-preserving, and the peer-focused revision directly honors the user's feedback. No boundary violations or drift were observed, so the interaction is a clear pass.
